newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks charge higher at midday as bonds rally.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks charge higher at midday as bonds rally.

text.p: U.S. stocks soared at midday Wednesday, driven higher by an exuberant bond market, fresh optimism over interest rates and inflation, and a growing belief that new proposals to balance the federal budget and cut taxes will be a long-term boost to financial markets.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 82 points, or around one percent, to 8256. Earlier, the New York Stock Exchange imposed curbs on index-arbitrage trading.
The long bond led the surge higher, with the benchmark 30-year Treasury surging 28/32 to a 6.32 percent yield.
The Nasdaq composite was up 12 points to 1584.

"Bonds are having a very good day and that helps stocks," said Barbara Marcin, vice president of Citibank Global Asset Management. "All recent information indicates we have low inflation and moderate growth...The balanced budget deal and the proposed capital gains tax cut are also driving stocks."
The market's strength was broad-based, with financial, drug and technology shares all gaining. Breadth on both the New York Stock Exchange and Nasdaq was positive.
Shares made large gains as the long bond yield dropped to 6.32 percent, its lowest level since March 1996.
"Both bonds and stocks have been working in absolute concert in a perfect market," said Dick Stein, vice president of U.S. Clearing Corp.
A heady combination of benign inflation, moderate economic growth and a balanced budget agreement served to propel financial markets higher, analysts said.
New home sales data for June and May confirmed the general thinking about the economy and gave an early lift to stocks, market-watchers said.

The Commerce Department said June new home sales rose 6.1 percent to an annual rate of 819,000. But analysts pointed to a sharp downward revision in the May figure, which now shows a one percent rise compared to the previous 7.1 percent gain.
"Housing stars were revised to a ridiculous degree in May," Stein said. "Combined, they both showed moderation."
But some analysts cautioned that markets still face the July employment report, due Friday.
Stocks and bonds also rose as the impact of the balanced budget deal between President Clinton and congressional Reblicans worked its way through the markets.
The deal was announced late Monday but the market has taken time to digest the details, analysts said.
The capital gains tax cut contained in the budget deal helped stocks, while bonds were lifted by hopes that a balanced budget would mean fewer government debt offerings.

"There is a demand for U.S. paper and supply is shrinking," said Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments. "Because the deficit is coming down, the goverment has less need to borrow."
Among particular stocks, Apple Computer Inc gained one point to 17-1/2.
Apple rose in active trade after persistent published reports and speculation on the Internet that company co-founder Steve Jobs will be named its next chairman.
Columbia/HCA Healthcare Corp was down 13/16 at 33-1/2 despite reporting strong second quarter results.

LAM Research Corp fell three to 53. The company reported a fourth quarter loss compared to a profit of $1.27 per share a year earlier. Merrill Lynch lowered its near-term rating on the stock to neutral from accumulate.
((--Wall Street Desk 212-859-1730))
